subject: Scope for prompt ephemeral storage & customer-data exclusion — DPIA follow-up

Subject: DPIA: prompt retention and training — initial questionnaire

Hi Monica,

Thanks for taking this on. Cardinal Health's privacy team is running a focused DPIA for third-party AI services that interact with patient-identifiable data. Attached is our latest questionnaire (finsec_questionnaire_v2.xlsx) — the items we need resolved quickly are sections 2 and 4: how prompts/responses are stored, for how long, and whether those artifacts are used for model training or tuning.

Specifically we need:
- A short, signed statement suitable for our audit: does Redwood ever use customer prompts/responses to train or fine-tune models by default?
- The retention windows for prompt/request logs, KV/prefix caches, and any secondary logging (error traces, debug dumps).
- A small diagram or summary of where ephemeral and persistent data live in Redwood's private and hosted deployments.

We have an internal audit cutoff of 2027-09-01 for our vendor evidence bundle. If you can provide a draft statement and the technical summary this week that would be ideal. Happy to hop on a quick call if that helps.

Best,
Sofia

Subject: Re: DPIA: prompt retention and training — initial questionnaire

Sofia / Monica — adding technical detail below and attaching compact notes. High level: Redwood does not include customer prompts/responses in any offline training pipelines by default. Customers can explicitly opt-in to contribute data for model improvement; that is an explict contract/feature and requires additional controls.

Short bullets for the questionnaire:
- Training use: NO by default. Customer data is not routed into model training or fine-tuning pipelines without an explicit opt-in agreement.
- Ephemeral caches: KV/prefix caches and inference caches are kept in-memory on serving nodes and persisted to encrypted local disk only for crash/restart safety. Persistence window for these safety snapshots is typically 6 hours and is rotated; not used for training.
- Request/response logs: Audit logs and request metadata (timestamps, model id, response token counts) are kept for 30 days in hosted by default; customers may shorten retention. Sensitive payload minimization is enabled on our API for flagged tokens.
- Debug traces: Full debug dumps (if collected) are stored under a customer incident bucket and retained per incident SLA (default: 90 days) and require elevated access.
- Private deployments: In VPC/on-prem installations all logs and caches remain within customer-controlled networking; Redwood can provide a configuration checklist for disabling any persistence for customers who require zero-on-disk storage.

Attachment: ephemeral_kv_cache_notes.md (technical note, 4 pages)

I can convert the bullets above into a one-paragraph signed statement for Sofia's audit pack; Monica, do you want to include me on the signature line or have a product-security signature?

— Rishi
Principal Engineer, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

[attachment: ephemeral_kv_cache_notes.md (md, 18KB)]

From: Sofia Alvarez <sofia.alvarez@finsec-consulting.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-08-19T08:09:00-07:00
Subject: Re: DPIA: prompt retention and training — initial questionnaire

Thanks Rishi — that's very helpful. Two quick clarifying items for the audit:
1) "Not used for training by default" is useful, but our auditors want an explicit signed sentence that spells out: "Redwood Inference does not use customer prompts or responses to train, fine-tune, or improve models unless a customer has explicitly opted in via a documented agreement."
2) For the hosted retention windows you listed (6 hours for crash snapshots, 30 days for request/response metadata), can you confirm if any backups or secondary replicas extend those windows (e.g., long-term backups, analytics copies) — auditors often find a hidden backup and flag it.

If you can provide the signed sentence and a compact matrix showing primary/secondary retention windows, we'll slot it into the DPIA and close this item.

Best,
Sofia

On a related note: Cardinal's legal team also asked for a short excerpt from your CAIQ showing encryption in transit and at rest; you mentioned you could share a snippet.

From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: DPIA: prompt retention and training — initial questionnaire

Sofia — attaching the items for your bundle. See attachments: redwood_no_training_statement.pdf (signed by me, Director of Customer Security & Trust), ephemeral_storage_matrix.csv (primary vs secondary retention windows), and caiq_response_excerpt.pdf (encryption controls excerpt).

Short answers here for reference:
- Signed line (excerpt): "Redwood Inference does not use customer prompts or responses to train, fine-tune, or improve models unless a customer has explicitly opted in via a documented agreement."
- Secondary/backup windows: Hosted primary logs and short-lived crash snapshots are retained as I described (6 hours for crash snapshots; 30 days for request metadata). We do not copy raw prompt/response payloads into long-term analytics stores or backups by default. Any analytics pipelines that require aggregated metrics operate on derived, anonymized metrics only; those aggregates are retained per our analytics retention policy (default 365 days).
- Private deployments: customer-controlled; Redwood provides a configuration checklist to enforce no-on-disk policies.

If Cardinal needs a formal attestation on company letterhead rather than a signed PDF, we can escalate to Legal and provide that before your 9/1 cutoff.

Cheers,
Monica Patel
Director, Customer Security & Trust
Redwood Inference
